speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are presenting with rectal bleeding and a palpable rectal mass; please describe exactly where you feel this mass and how the bleeding has presented. REQUEST TEST: Digital_Rectal_Exam.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: A palpable, non-tender, prolapsed mass that can be easily pushed back into the anal sphincter by the examiner's finger.

speaker: Patient
text: 45-year-old female. The patient reports a 2-week history of rectal bleeding occurring daily with bowel movements. She denies any pain with defecation and does not present with any other complaints.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rectal bleeding daily with bowel movements. I also have No pain with defecation. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing that. While I will rely on my own examination to guide my assessment, could you tell me if you have any history of travel to areas where tuberculosis is endemic or recent close contact with someone who has an active infection? REQUEST TEST: Digital_Rectal_Exam.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: A palpable, non-tender, prolapsed mass that can be easily pushed back into the anal sphincter by the examiner's finger.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Rectal Prolapse. The examination findings of a non-tender, prolapsed mass reducible by the finger are classic for rectal prolapse, which explains the rectal bleeding due to mucosal irritation. While you mentioned a previous opinion of tuberculosis, the physical exam does not support this diagnosis.
